svg.text: THE MOUNTAINS: ONE SKI MOUNTAIN, FROM MOUNT OLYMPUS DOWN TO THE SKI LODGE
The plan on paper. Nothing is built yet. North is up. One box = one plot (42 m, 12 x 12 squares). The big number = the plot's height in metres over the Lodge Yard.

97 plots (68 stand today, the rest are new). The summit stands 112 m over the base. * = a plot that stands today and moves here. Mount Shasta is gone as a name: its plots are the middle of the mountain.
THE NORTH POLE (its own room, at the end of the Polar Trail)
Plan: the Workshop up on a hill,
the square down in the middle,
a sled hill you ride down to the
● green: easy, wide, near the base (up to 13 %)
■ blue: the middle of the mountain (13 to 27 %)
◆ black: steep, narrower, trees and bumps (27 to 41 %)
◆◆ double black: off the summit, chutes and cliffs (over 41 %)
a lift: it carries you up, station to station
a main walking way, 3 squares, laid on the squares
ONE RIDE, TOP TO BOTTOM: the Top Station beside the temples to the Ski Lodge. 462 m long, 112 m down, never uphill. About 35 seconds on the board.
The summit is Mount Olympus. Its temples stay on top; the Top Station stands
beside them. Four double blacks drop off the summit. Under them eight blacks,
then eight blues, then seven greens that end at the Lodge or a lift.
Runs fork and merge; every run ends at a lift or the base.
The pistes (wide open snow), the base village, the mid station and its lake,
The Ski Lodge, Rentals, the Ski Patrol, an inn and a shop on the Village Street,
the Mid Station, the Top Station, the Warming Hut, the bath house, the Temple.
